topics.label: Introduction to the lecture on inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the audience and frames the lecture's focus on how previously introduced immune components work together.

topics.label: Recognition of danger by innate pattern-recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immunity detects PAMPs and DAMPs, what makes PAMPs useful, and how pattern-recognition receptors are encoded and positioned to recognize them.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signaling
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics describe how TLRs detect microbial material and how their location and signaling direct the resulting immune response.

topics.label: Other pattern-recognition pathways and inflammasome-driven inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics extend innate danger sensing beyond TLRs and explain how inflammasome activation can drive inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics show how local detection of infection triggers sentinel-cell signals that recruit leukocytes to the affected tissue.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and dendritic cell migration for adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells and tissue fluid travel through lymphatic drainage to lymph nodes, where adaptive immune cells can be activated.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how excessive inflammatory signaling can spread systemically and cause septic shock.

topics.label: Turning off inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains passive and active mechanisms that reduce or stop inflammation.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics describe the fate of inflamed tissue after injury, including repair and the containment of persistent inflammation.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and identifies the subject of the next lecture.
